description: Hello! We are a team of space enthusiasts and technology lovers participating in the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. Our goal is to make space exploration more interesting and accessible through technology and creativity. We enjoy learning about NASA missions and sharing the stories of spacecraft, rovers, and scientific discoveries. Through our project, Space Relics Explorer, we hope to inspire students and young minds to explore space, discover new things, and stay curious about the universe.
summary:
Space exploration leaves behind more than just discoveries. When missions end, spacecraft, rovers, landers, and scientific instruments can remain on the Moon, Mars, or travel far beyond our solar system. Although these machines may no longer be active, the stories behind them are still worth remembering.

That is what inspired me to create **Space Relics Explorer**. It is an interactive website where people can explore the solar system in 3D and discover the NASA missions and equipment that were left behind. Visitors can learn about different missions, explore their history, and follow important moments through timelines.

From the Apollo equipment on the Moon to the rovers on Mars and spacecraft travelling through deep space, the project brings these stories together in one place.

My goal is simple: to help people see that a mission does not lose its importance just because it has ended. Every piece of equipment left behind represents years of hard work, scientific progress, and human curiosity. Through Space Relics Explorer, I want to make sure those stories are not forgotten.
details:
About Space Relics Explorer

Space Relics Explorer started with a simple question: what happens to the machines and equipment we send into space after their missions are over?

We often hear about famous space missions, their discoveries, and the people behind them. But we do not always pay attention to the spacecraft, rovers, landers, and scientific instruments that remain behind after those missions end. I wanted to create something that would make these forgotten parts of space exploration easier and more interesting to discover.

Space Relics Explorer is an interactive website that brings these stories together. Visitors can explore a 3D view of the solar system, move between different areas, discover NASA missions, and learn about the equipment that remains on the Moon, Mars, and in deep space.

The project includes missions and equipment such as the Apollo lunar equipment, Surveyor 3, Sojourner, Spirit, Opportunity, InSight, Ingenuity, Voyager 1 and 2, Pioneer 10, Cassini, and New Horizons. Each entry helps visitors understand what the mission was designed to do, what it achieved, and what happened to its equipment after the mission ended.

I built the website using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, with Three.js powering the interactive 3D experience. I also worked on the visual design, navigation, mission information, and timelines to make the experience easier to explore.

As an independent developer, I wanted this project to be more than just a collection of facts. I wanted visitors to feel like they were exploring the history of space missions themselves.

Space Relics Explorer is my way of showing that even when a mission comes to an end, its contribution to science and exploration remains. The equipment may be silent, but the stories behind it are still worth telling.
